blocks.text: DCS generates about 200,000 forms each month from approximately 3,500 templates, on Central Pro and Output Designer software that has been unsupported since June 2010. This proposal sets out how [PARTNER LEGAL NAME] will work with your staff to replace that software with Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Forms, convert the approximately 300 XFT forms hosted by the FormsGen screen in SEMS, put the online application for services in front of customers through a portal, and leave your team able to build the next forms themselves.

We will deliver four things. First, a forms platform in your Adobe-managed environment, with the templates, themes, fragments and data model that every form and document draws on [1]. Second, document generation that takes over from Central Pro: templates designed in Forms Designer, generated on demand and in batch, converted to PDF/A and archived [2]. Third, the online application for services as an adaptive form on a customer portal, with drafts, submissions and data exchanged with SEMS [3]. Fourth, Acrobat Sign set up, demonstrated and documented, with DSHS branding [4].

Alongside the build we will deliver the 200 hours of training the RFP asks for, to the 8 to 12 staff you name, so that conversion and form development continue in your hands. Where the RFP reaches past what Adobe documents on the pages we checked, or past what our service catalog covers, we say so in section 3 and list the item in section 11 as custom work or as a point to confirm with Adobe.
What makes this response different

items: Sourced Adobe facts. Every statement about what an Adobe product does carries a number that points to the Adobe page it rests on.
A named service for every requirement. Section 9 answers each line of the RFP's scope and deliverables, and section 5 lists the services that deliver them.
Planning hours that carry into a statement of work. The contract's Statement of Work starts from the same list of services and hours you evaluate.

Gaps stated plainly. Legacy conversion tooling, the forms history front end, mainframe specifics, Intelligent Mail Barcode, FedRAMP and training topics outside AEM Forms are each marked as custom work or as a point to confirm with Adobe.
Training inside the delivery. DCS staff convert forms beside our team from the first wave and lead the later waves.

blocks.text: SEMS is the mission-critical case management system for Washington's child support program, and form generation is a major part of it: staff and automated batch processes produce the forms that support establishing and collecting support orders. That system was built around Central Pro and Output Designer in 2004. Replacing them is the first step in modernizing forms generation, and the replacement has to give DCS similar functional processes, products and outcomes, integrated into SEMS.

We read the RFP as four linked pieces of work: replace the generation engine and the design tools, convert the forms with your staff, open a first online form to customers, and transfer the knowledge to keep going. DCS provides overall project management. We provide a Project Lead, manage our own staff and deliverables, and work inside the Adobe-managed hosting that DCS is purchasing.

blocks.text: 3.1 Forms platform and architecture

AEM Forms is Adobe's solution to create, manage, publish and update complex digital forms, integrating the submitted data with back-end processes and business rules and saving it in an external data store [3]. We will set up the Forms solution with the Communications add-on that generates documents, add your users to the Forms groups on Author and Publish, and set up the development kit and project that developers deploy from [1].

On that base we will build the adaptive form templates, the theme that carries the DSHS brand and the reusable fragments every form starts from [5]. New adaptive forms will use Adaptive Forms Core Components, which Adobe recommends for new forms [6]. Print templates will be XDP form designs created in Forms Designer, each with the XML data it merges defined [2]. Together these take the place of Output Designer and Form Designer. With your staff we will write the forms architecture, deployment architecture, technical design and building blocks documents the RFP names.

blocks.title: Decision for DCS and Adobe: deployment and front-end approach
blocks.text: Our catalog and the Adobe pages we cite describe AEM Forms as a Cloud Service. The RFP describes an Adobe-managed environment in the Amazon Web Services Government Cloud and names Interactive Communications, the Agent UI, document fragments, watched folders and AEM Workbench. Whether each is available depends on the version and deployment Adobe provides to DCS, and our checked sources do not cover them. We will confirm this with Adobe and DCS before the technical design is drafted, and record there the front-end decision the RFP asks for: Interactive Communications or adaptive forms.
3.2 Converting the legacy forms estate

Conversion starts with analysis. For each template we will record, with your staff, what the RFP's design list asks for: variables, logical and common sections, required and optional sections, repeating data, parent and child relationships, pagination, barcodes, images and rendition sizes. The resulting conversion workbook drives the schema, the fragment library and the order of work. Each form then takes one of three routes:

items: Automated conversion. Adobe's Automated Forms Conversion service converts existing PDF forms (AcroForms, XFA-based or non-interactive) in batches within the service's size limits. We review and correct each converted form and apply your template and theme. The service produces forms on Foundation Components, the earlier of Adobe's two component sets for adaptive forms, so those forms are maintained with that set's editor [7].

Rebuild on Core Components. Forms that need new logic are rebuilt with panels, steps, fields and validation [6], and with rules that trigger actions on fields based on conditions, user inputs and user actions [8].
Print templates. Letters and notices that are generated, not filled in, become XDP form designs in Forms Designer [2].

blocks.text: Neither our catalog nor the Adobe pages we checked describe a tool that reads XFT, IFD or MDF files directly. We will test conversion on the sample InForm files DCS provides. Where no tooling path exists, the form is rebuilt by hand from its analysis, which is custom work sized in discovery.

We convert the first wave with your staff observing and reviewing, share the second, and from the third wave your staff convert while we review and coach. The same pattern supports the DSHS team in creating up to 1,500 XDP templates.

blocks.title: Key assumption: who converts what
blocks.text: We assume the approximately 300 forms are converted jointly, in waves, and that the up to 1,500 XDP templates are designed and laid out by DSHS staff with our support, as the RFP words it. If DCS expects the bidder to produce the 1,500 templates, the effort in section 5 changes materially.
3.3 The online application and customer portal

The application for services will be one multi-step adaptive form on Core Components: panels and steps, fields, validation, and rules that show, hide, calculate and call services [6]. It will sit on AEM Sites pages, using the Adaptive Forms Container and Embed components that AEM Forms provides [9]. Forms placed with the Embed component do not get Sites versioning, targeting, translation or multi-site management, so we will decide placement form by form.

The portal will use the Forms Portal components (Search and Lister, Drafts and Submissions, and Link) so a customer can find the application, save a draft, return to it and see what was submitted. Drafts and submissions are held in your Azure Storage account through the Unified Storage Connector, and only signed-in people can resume drafts and see their submissions [10]. One theme will style both the pages and the forms on them [11]. We will also build up to 15 editable templates for the Web Channel [5].

Each submitted application will produce a Submission PDF (Document of Record), auto-generated or on a branded XDP template bound to the form's fields [12]. Submit actions will be set so that data lands in a store DCS owns, with server-side revalidation turned on [13]. Before release we will review the form against the accessibility standard DCS names, using the checks Adobe lists for form authors [14].

For responses that depend on form content, such as the packet number, we will build AEM Workflow models that start when a form is submitted, assign review tasks, route approvals and rejections, and send email notifications [15]. The emailed link with a specific token that lets a recipient return to the portal and respond is not a documented product feature in our sources. We will design it as custom work with your security staff.
3.4 Data integration with SEMS

We will configure the data sources (REST, SOAP or OData services, or a relational database) and build the Form Data Model that prefills forms from the case system and writes submitted data back to it [16]. This covers the RFP's develop items: a data source for a RESTful service, a form data model for it, and its objects, services and relationships. We will deliver the two prefill services for adaptive forms, the schema design and definitions document, and sample XML data files for testing.

The update mainframe workflow will call a REST web service through the Form Data Model or a submit action to a REST endpoint [13]. We assume DCS builds and exposes the REST services in front of SEMS and its mainframe, and owns their security and transaction rules. Our catalog holds nothing specific to mainframe integration, so that interface is specified jointly in the technical design.
3.5 Document generation, batch and archive

To take over from Central Pro behind the SEMS forms generation front end, we will set up server-to-server credentials and connect your application to the synchronous Communications APIs, so a letter or PDF is generated from a template and data the moment a form is submitted or a case worker asks for it [2]. For overnight and volume work we will connect your Microsoft Azure Storage, create the batch data store and batch configurations, and set up the scheduled runs that turn a set of records into PDF or print documents [17]. Generated PDFs can be converted to PDF/A and validated, and document packages assembled or split with DDX [2]. We will also create up to 15 XDP templates for the Print Channel.

3.6 E-signature with Acrobat Sign

Acrobat Sign is Adobe's digital signature service, which lets people sign documents electronically and lets you collect signatures [18]. We will create the Acrobat Sign API application and the cloud configuration on Author and Publish, then add signing to your process with the Sign Document workflow step: the signers, the signing order and the signed document [4]. Forms on Core Components sign through that workflow step. Forms on Foundation Components, such as those produced by automated conversion, can carry signing in the form itself, with signers and their order, signer authentication and Acrobat Sign fields placed in the document [19].

In Acrobat Sign we will set up groups with their own settings, branding and templates, administrators, users and sign-in [20], and configure company name, logo and email branding, signature preferences, send and security settings, and the external archive that receives a copy of every signed agreement [21]. That configuration is the DSHS brand and graphics demonstration. Agreements DCS sends often become library templates [22] and workflow templates in the Custom Workflow Designer [23]. Every document passes through milestones that are documented in an audit report for every transaction [24].

We will demonstrate to agency staff, and document, sending a document to a single signer and to multiple signers in a set order. Self-signing is not described in our catalog, so we will confirm it on DCS's Acrobat Sign account before the session.
3.7 Security, hosting and access

DCS is purchasing Adobe-managed hosting, which Adobe intends to deploy in a separate environment in the Amazon Web Services Government Cloud with FedRAMP compliance. We will work inside that environment and configure what Adobe gives DCS access to configure. Our checked sources show that Adobe's Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO 9001, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 22301 and CSA STAR Level 2 for Adobe Experience Cloud, which includes AEM Sites [25]. They do not cover the FedRAMP status or the configuration of the environment Adobe is providing to DCS, so we make no statement about either. Both are for Adobe to confirm to DCS in writing.

items: Internal users. Users are added to the Forms groups on Author and Publish [1]. For AEM as a Cloud Service, Adobe sign-in covers authors, administrators and developers, not a site's visitors [26]. Active Directory sign-in and the LDAP, user group and access control list setup the RFP lists depend on the managed environment and are confirmed with Adobe in design.
External users. The portal needs signed-in users [10]. Sign-in through Secure Access Washington is integration work designed with DCS, WaTech and Adobe. Our catalog does not cover it.
Processing controls. Forms-centric workflows give consistent and auditable processing with role-based access control [3], and sensitive workflow data can be kept in your own storage [15].
Data location. Application data, drafts, submissions and archived documents are held in stores DCS owns [13].
Email. Workflow steps send email notifications [15]. The SMTP configuration of the managed environment is set with Adobe.

blocks.title: Three training topics to confirm
blocks.text: The RFP asks for training on a web-based DITA component content management editor, on AEM Workbench with JEE applications, and on installing AEM. Our catalog covers none of them, and each depends on the products DCS licenses and the deployment Adobe provides. We ask DCS and Adobe to confirm whether each is in scope (section 12).

The DCS Project Manager leads the project. Our Project Lead, [PROJECT LEAD NAME], is the single point of contact, manages all bidder staff and services, and attends agency meetings to present status as directed.

items: Schedule. Prepared in Microsoft Project and maintained through the project. It shows tasks and timelines for each deliverable, milestones, critical path tasks, our personnel with skills and dates, and the agency personnel we need.
Work Plan. It sets out the process and procedures for deliverables, instructions and checklists for onsite services, our methodology with an estimate of agency resources, and the closeout procedure.

Status reports. Every other Monday, in the format the agency approves: accomplishments, critical issues, personnel utilized, items planned for the next period, and issues and risks with mitigation strategies.
Quality assurance. With agency staff we develop and run tests for letter templates, fragments and schemas, and for each workflow the RFP lists. Unit test results are documented and delivered.
Converted templates. DCS provides testing scenarios and sample files. We assist with testing, and DCS tests the generated forms before signing off on user acceptance.

Acceptance. A deliverable is accepted only when the DCS Project Manager approves it in writing. The agency has five business days to accept or reject, and we have five business days to correct and return a rejected deliverable.
Personnel. Key personnel do not change except as requested or approved by DSHS. Any proposed substitution is submitted to DCS in writing.

Closeout. The Project Closeout document summarizes major accomplishments, the deliverables checklist, performance to schedule and to budget, satisfaction and acceptance of all project services, lessons learned, and outstanding risks or issues.

sections.title: What we need from you, and open questions

blocks.text: To complete this response

items: Attachment D, the Bidder Response Form, is a separate Word file that was not in the document we read. It holds the scored questions, the administrative questions and the pricing questions. Every question must be answered in that form, in order. This proposal does not replace it.

Attachment B (Bid Submission Letter) and Attachment C (Bidder Certifications and Assurances) must be signed, unaltered, by a person authorized to bind [PARTNER LEGAL NAME]. The letter must disclose any current or former state employees employed by or subcontracted with the bidder.
The partner must complete the pricing at [HOURLY RATE], travel costs, the additional training rate, the Executive Order 18-03 certification, the proprietary pages statement and the references.
Section D mentions an Attachment E that is not in the RFP's list of attachments. Ask the Coordinator whether it exists.
No DSHS client information may appear in the response.

blocks.text: Open questions for DCS

items: Which AEM Forms version and deployment will Adobe provide, and what may the contractor configure in it?
Is the target front end Interactive Communications, adaptive forms, or both?
Of the approximately 3,500 templates in use, which make up the approximately 300 XFT forms and the up to 1,500 XDP templates, and who converts each group?
Is automated conversion to Foundation Components acceptable for forms with little logic, or should all forms be rebuilt on Core Components?
What REST services exist in front of SEMS today, and who builds the ones this project needs?
Is the archive Azure Storage, a Cosmos database, SQL storage, or a combination?
Does SDP in the deliverables list mean XDP, as in the scope?
Are a DITA content management editor, AEM Workbench and installing AEM in scope for training?
Which accessibility standard and which languages apply?

blocks.title: Our commitment
blocks.text: If awarded, we will contact the DCS Project Manager within five business days of contract execution, hold the kick-off within ten business days, and bring these open questions to that session with a proposed owner for each.
